title: Read legacy Rails and prove a safe change
outcome: Map a production-style feature, write behavior tests, and explain a change without copying work code.
book: Eloquent Ruby ch. 29; Metaprogramming Ruby part II
cue: Trace one path. Break one promise. Prove one repair.

exercises.title: Find and fix the bug
exercises.prompt: A test passes using a fake repository but real requests enqueue receipts twice. What boundaries must you investigate?

exercises.title: Change one condition
exercises.prompt: You upgrade a small component toward modern Ruby/Rails. What is your first compatibility checklist?

trace.title: Route entry
trace.detail: Start a legacy feature investigation at its entry point. Find the route, controller action, service, model/query, callbacks, worker, and response presenter. Draw only the path relevant to the reported behavior. Search for callers before changing a method contract.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
Capstone: a task can be completed by an allowed member. It creates a receipt intent once. A worker sends it later. Add a list page with owner names. Show access denial, validation failure, concurrent completion, provider timeout, and a bounded query count.

Write a two-minute explanation: what enters, what rule holds, which writes commit together, what can repeat, and how you verified it. Keep a bug diary with symptom → cause → smallest fix → regression test.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail: A broad rescue in a controller can hide a service failure as a 200. A mocked model can make a callback-heavy feature look simpler than it is. Read the callback registrations and SQL behavior before judging coverage.

recallPrompt: Without notes: Map a production-style feature, write behavior tests, and explain a change without copying work code. Give a concrete failure example.
